# Documentation Overview

This skill provides patterns for creating legally sound employment documentation: **offer letters, employment contracts, employee handbooks/policies, NDAs, and non-compete/related agreements**.

## Document Types Covered

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Communicates initial job offer, position, compensation, contingencies, at-will status | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal binding agreement with detailed terms (IP, confidentiality, non-compete, severance, termination) | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies, procedures, code of conduct, PTO/benefits | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality obligations | Before access to sensitive info |
| **Non-Compete** | Restricts competition after employment | Hire/Exit (where legal) |

## Key Legal Considerations

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

**DISCLAIMER: These templates are for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice. Consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.**

# Recommended Workflow for Creating an Offer Letter

Here is the step-by-step workflow to produce a complete, customized offer letter:

1. **Identify role and classification**
   - Job title, department, reporting structure, start date
   - Full-time vs. part-time, exempt vs. non-exempt (determine under FLSA and state law)
   - Location/remote status

2. **Confirm compensation package**
   - Base salary/pay rate and pay frequency
   - Bonus eligibility and structure
   - Equity details (type, vesting schedule, cliff)
   - Benefits eligibility (health, 401(k), PTO, holidays)

3. **Gather required contingencies**
   - Background check requirements
   - Right-to-work/immigration verification
   - Required signed documents (NDA, IP assignment, non-compete if applicable/permitted)
   - Any credential/degree verification

4. **Determine at-will vs. contract status**
   - Add/confirm at-will language if applicable by jurisdiction

5. **Customize template**
   - Fill all placeholders with role-specific details
   - Adjust duties/skills sections for a senior software engineer (see customization notes below)
   - Add jurisdiction-specific language as required by local counsel

6. **Legal review** — have employment counsel review before sending

7. **Route for approval & send**
   - Obtain required internal signatories (hiring manager, comp, HR)
   - Issue letter with an expiration deadline
   - Track acceptance and return of signed copy

# Offer Letter Template

Because you specified **senior software engineer**, I've added customization notes throughout and an optional technical section. All bracketed `[X]` items are placeholders you must fill in.

```markdown
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [DATE]

[Candidate Name]
[Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Dear [Candidate Name],

We are pleased to extend an offer of employment for the position of **Senior
Software Engineer** at [COMPANY NAME]. We believe your skills and experience
will be valuable additions to our team.

## Position Details

**Title:** Senior Software Engineer
**Department:** [Engineering / R&D]
**Reports To:** [Engineering Manager Name / Title]
**Location:** [Office Location / Remote / Hybrid]
**Start Date:** [Proposed Start Date]
**Employment Type:** [Full-Time/Part-Time], [Exempt/Non-Exempt]

## Responsibilities (customize for the role)

*Example bullet points for a senior engineer — tailor to your actual role:*

- Design, develop, and maintain [technology stack, e.g., distributed systems / 
  web applications / mobile APIs / backend services]
- Lead technical design discussions and contribute to architecture decisions
- Mentor and provide technical guidance to less senior engineers
- Write clean, readable, well-tested code and participate in code reviews
- Collaborate with product, design, and cross-functional teams to deliver
  features on roadmap
- [Other duties specific to your posting]

## Compensation

**Base Salary:** $[AMOUNT] per [year/hour], paid [bi-weekly/semi-monthly/monthly]
**Bonus:** [Eligible for annual bonus of up to X% based on company and individual
performance / Not applicable]
**Equity:** [X shares of stock options vesting over 4 years with 1-year cliff /
Not applicable]

> *Senior engineering roles often include equity; specify exercise price,
> vesting schedule, and reference the company stock option plan.*

## Benefits

You will be eligible for our standard benefits package, including:
- Health insurance (medical, dental, vision) effective [date]
- 401(k) with [X]% company match
- [X] days paid time off per year
- [X] paid holidays
- [Other benefits, e.g., professional development stipend, remote stipend]

Full details will be provided during onboarding.

## Contingencies

This offer is contingent upon:
- Successful completion of [background check / reference checks]
- Verification of your right to work in [Country]
- Execution of required employment documents including:
  - Confidentiality Agreement
  - [Non-Compete Agreement, WHERE LEGALLY PERMISSIBLE in your jurisdiction]
  - [IP Assignment Agreement — especially important for software roles]

> **Note:** In many jurisdictions a non-compete cannot be a condition of
> employment, and its scope/duration is strictly limited. Review with counsel
> before including. In California and several other U.S. states, non-competes
> are effectively unenforceable.

## At-Will Employment

Please note that employment with [Company Name] is at-will. This means that
either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any time,
with or without cause or notice. This offer letter does not constitute a
contract of employment for any specific period.

[Omit or customize only if hiring in a jurisdiction that does not permit
at-will language.]

## Acceptance

To accept this offer, please sign below and return by [DEADLINE DATE]. This
offer will expire if not accepted by that date.

We are excited about the possibility of you joining our team. If you have any
questions, please contact [HR Contact] at [email/phone].

Sincerely,

_________________________
[Hiring Manager Name]
[Title]
[Company Name]

---

## ACCEPTANCE

I accept this offer of employment and agree to the terms stated above.

Signature: _________________________

Printed Name: _________________________

Date: _________________________

Anticipated Start Date: _________________________
```

# Best Practices — Do's & Don'ts

### Do's
- **Consult legal counsel** — employment law varies significantly by state/country
- **Keep signed copies** on file
- **Customize for jurisdiction**, role, and seniority level
- **Be specific** about compensation, equity vesting, and start date
- **Time-limit the offer** and track responses

### Don'ts
- **Don't use the template unchanged** — customize every field
- **Don't make promises** beyond what policies or plans can support (creates implied contracts)
- **Don't include discriminatory language**
- **Don't skip at-will language** where it applies
- **Don't include overly broad restrictive covenants** (non-competes, NDAs) — they invite legal challenges and are often invalid
- **Don't send without legal review**, especially for technical/equity-heavy roles

---

# Reminders for a Senior Software Engineer Offer

- **IP Assignment is critical** — software work product clauses must be clear; include a prior inventions exhibit so the candidate can carve out pre-existing IP.
- **Equity details matter** — be explicit about option count, exercise price, vesting schedule, cliff, and whether any acceleration applies on change of control.
- **Remote-work/geographic tax implications** — if the candidate is in a different state/country than the company, both employment law and tax registration issues may arise; confirm compliance before extending the offer.
- **Non-compete scope** — an enforceable restriction (where allowed at all) should be modest in duration (typically ≤ 12 months) and limited to genuinely competitive, similar businesses — not "across all industries."
